title: Nutmeg Nicely Napped Greek Duck Legs Galaktoboureko
description: A citrusy, crumbly, date-night Greek dish featuring duck legs, fermented jang, and crispy galaktoboureko pastry. This halal-friendly recipe is perfect for a special occasion.
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the honey, lemon juice, and lemon zest to create a marinade.
Place the duck legs in a large zip-top plastic bag or a shallow dish, and pour the marinade over them.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight, turning the legs occasionally.
In a large skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of the butter over medium-high heat, and sear the duck legs until browned on both sides.
Transfer the duck legs to a baking dish, and roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, or until cooked through.
While the duck legs are cooking, prepare the galaktoboureko pastry by mixing together the flour, breadcrumbs, and egg in a large bowl.
Add the milk, yeast, vanilla extract, and brown sugar to the bowl, and stir to combine.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on the size of your duck legs.
Place a duck leg in the center of each piece of dough, and brush the edges with the remaining butter.
Fold the dough over the duck leg, and press the edges together to seal the pastry.
Place the galaktoboureko on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Serve the duck legs hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a side of tangy fermented jang sauce, if desired.
